Data Storage & External Services

The website persists catalog, order, cart, raincheck, and identity data in SQL Server through Entity Framework. Recommendations can be requested from an Azure Machine Learning endpoint; OWIN authentication is configured for external OAuth providers, and telemetry is sent through the Application Insights provider.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • The application is a single web project with MVC and Web API surfaces sharing an Entity Framework context.
  • Unity provides dependency injection for application services and the shared HTTP client.
  • Database schema deployment is represented separately by a SQL project and deployment scripts.

DTOs & Contracts

The Web API returns domain types such as Product and Raincheck; the MVC UI uses view models including ShoppingCartViewModel and OrderDetailsViewModel. Order is the checkout form model. No immutable DTO convention, protobuf schema, GraphQL schema, or separate OpenAPI source file was identified; Swagger is configured in the application. Newtonsoft.Json handles JSON serialization and deserialization.

Communication Patterns

  • Browser-to-website communication uses synchronous HTTP requests; API responses are JSON and MVC responses are HTML.
  • Controllers and query services use direct method calls and Entity Framework access to the shared SQL Server database.
  • The recommendation engine makes a synchronous HTTP request to an Azure Machine Learning endpoint through an injected HttpClient.
  • ASP.NET Identity uses OWIN cookie authentication and configured external OAuth providers. Checkout is protected with [Authorize]; the API controllers do not show explicit authorization attributes. TLS depends on deployment configuration and was not established from the source project.
  • No message broker, service discovery, API gateway, retry policy, circuit breaker, or client-side load balancing was identified.

Core Business Workflows

PartsUnlimited supports an online retail experience for browsing products, managing a shopping cart, and placing orders. Store administrators manage catalog and raincheck information, while an optional recommendation integration supplies related-product suggestions.

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
PartsUnlimitedWebsiteCatalog and shoppingProduct, Category, CartItemSQL Server
PartsUnlimitedWebsiteSales and customer identityOrder, OrderDetail, ApplicationUserSQL Server and ASP.NET Identity
PartsUnlimitedWebsiteStore operationsRaincheck, StoreSQL Server
Recommendation integrationProduct recommendationsNo local entity ownershipAzure Machine Learning endpoint

The application is a single deployable website with a shared database; the contexts above are logical groupings, not separate services.

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Browse and add a product to the cart

  1. A shopper opens the catalog or a category page.
  2. The store controller queries products and categories through the shared EF context.
  3. The shopper requests an add-to-cart action; the application resolves the product and current cart.
  4. The cart updates its item collection and persists the change.
  5. The cart summary is recalculated and returned to the shopper.

Workflow 2: Submit an order

  1. An authenticated shopper submits the checkout form.
  2. The checkout controller checks the configured promo code and obtains the shopper identity from the authenticated principal.
  3. The order and cart contents are associated, then saved through the shared context.
  4. The shopper is redirected to an order-completion view that verifies the order belongs to that username.

Workflow 3: Get product recommendations

  1. A product page requests recommendations when the ShowRecommendations setting is enabled.
  2. The recommendation engine calls the configured Azure Machine Learning endpoint with the product identifier.
  3. Returned product identifiers are resolved against the local catalog and displayed as recommendations.

Cross-Service Data Flows

There is no multi-service gateway aggregation. The recommendation integration sends a product identifier to an external Azure Machine Learning endpoint; the returned identifiers are matched against the website's SQL-backed product catalog. If the external request fails, the recommendation engine catches an HTTP request exception and yields an empty recommendation set.

Business Workflow Sequence

sequenceDiagram participant Shopper participant Checkout as "Checkout Controller" participant Cart as "Shopping Cart" participant Context as "Entity Framework Context" participant Db as "SQL Server" Shopper->>Checkout: Submit checkout form Checkout->>Checkout: Check promo code and authenticated user alt Promo code is valid Checkout->>Cart: Create order from current cart Cart->>Context: Add order details and update cart Checkout->>Context: Save changes Context->>Db: Persist order and details Db-->>Context: Saved order identifier Context-->>Checkout: Order saved Checkout-->>Shopper: Redirect to order completion else Promo code is invalid Checkout-->>Shopper: Redisplay checkout form end

Business Rules & Decision Logic

  • Checkout requires an authenticated user and the configured promo code; the checked-in implementation compares against a fixed demonstration code.
  • The order username and date are assigned by the server, rather than accepted from the submitted form.
  • The completion action queries by both order identifier and current username.
  • Shipping is computed per item. The default calculator applies a standard tax rate with a different rate for postal codes beginning with 98; a separate cart-removal response computes totals inline.
  • Product and order model validation attributes constrain required fields and ranges; detailed persistence mappings are documented in data-architecture.md.
  • Order persistence is performed through Entity Framework save operations. No cross-service transaction, message-based choreography, or business audit trail was identified.

Version & Compatibility Risks

The application targets .NET Framework 4.5.1 and uses older ASP.NET MVC, Web API, OWIN, and Newtonsoft.Json packages. These versions are legacy and should be evaluated for support and compatibility as part of any runtime or framework modernization. The standard dotnet list package dependency-tree command could not load this legacy project on the current Linux host, so the inventory uses direct package declarations only.

Notable Observations

  • Package versions are pinned in PartsUnlimitedWebsite/packages.config; no lock file was found.
  • Entity Framework 6 is used with a separate SQL Server database project and migration scripts.
  • Swashbuckle and Web API expose an API-documentation surface.
  • No test-scoped NuGet dependencies or separate test project were identified.

Caching Strategy

The application uses System.Runtime.Caching.MemoryCache for selected product, latest-product, and top-selling-product data. Observed entries generally expire after ten minutes; the cache is process-local. No distributed cache, database second-level cache, or explicit cache-coordination mechanism was identified.

Data Ownership Boundaries

The MVC and Web API surfaces share the same website project, context, and SQL Server database; there is no database-per-service or cross-service database access. The database project manages schema deployment, and EF query services provide data access for application flows. No CQRS or event-driven persistence boundary was identified.
